Article 10

1. Other violence as referred to in Article 4 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
2. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether or not using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
3. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 33. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 34. Protection of women is any effort made to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. 36. Implementation of Child Protection is a series of activities carried out by the Regional Government, community, and parents, aimed at preventing, reducing risks, and handling victims of acts of violence, exploitation, abuse and neglect of children. 37. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, be healthy, intelligent, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination. 38. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic, social exploitation including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 39. Violence Against Children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, and psychologically. 40. Child Abuse is any action against a child, including placing the child in a situation that can cause adverse effects on the welfare, safety, dignity and development of the child. 43. Assistance is social work that has professional competence in its field. 44. Child Neglect is any act of neglecting the fulfillment of basic needs, care, and maintenance that interferes with or hinders the growth and development of children, including leaving children in dangerous situations. 45. Prevention is the effort of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, abuse, exploitation and neglect of children. 46. Risk Reduction is early action towards children and their families who are in vulnerable situations or at risk of experiencing various forms of violence, abuse, exploitation, and neglect. 47. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of children who are victims of violence, abuse, exploitation, and or neglect. 48. Care Environment is care by parents and care outside parental care. 57. CHAPTER XII

SANCTIONS

Article 32

In the event of violence against Women and Children, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 16

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 13 letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 5

Physical violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

Article 6

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 4 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.

6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb. 12. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the State. 13. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 15. Children in Need of Special Protection hereinafter abbreviated as AMPK are Children in need of special protection. 19. Street child is a child whose life is irregular by spending most of his/her time outside the home to earn a living on the streets or in public places. 22. Gifted child is a child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 24. Child in conflict with the law is a child in conflict with the law, a child who is a victim of a criminal act, and a child who is a witness to a criminal act. 25. Adopted Child is a Child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the Family of Parents, legal Guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education and raising of the Child into the environment of the Family of adoptive Parents based on a court decision or determination. 26. Foster Child is a Child who is cared for by a person or institution to be provided with guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health because the Parents or one of the Parents is unable to guarantee the proper growth and development of the Child. 27. Child economically exploited is an action with or without the consent of the child who is a victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual exploitation, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of children by other parties to obtain material benefits. 28. Child sexually exploited is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of children to obtain benefits, including but limited to all activities of prostitution and sexual abuse. 29. Child labor is children both boys and girls who are involved in economic activities that interfere with or hinder the growth and development process and are dangerous to the physical and mental health of children. 30. Custody is the power of Parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect and develop Children in accordance with the religion they profess and in accordance with their abilities, talents, and interests. 31. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government and regional government. 32.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs and the interests of the local community on its own initiative based on community aspirations within the system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 2. Regional Government is the administration of government affairs by the regional government and DPRD according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration of Tanggamus Regency 4. Regent is the Regent of Tanggamus
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Tanggamus Regency
6. Regional Apparatus abbreviated as PD is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives of Tanggamus Regency in the administration of Government Affairs which are the authority of Tanggamus Regency. 7. Regional Planning, Development, Research and Innovation Agency hereinafter abbreviated as Bapperida is the Regional Planning, Development, Research and Innovation Agency in Tanggamus Regency. 8. Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA DALDUK and KB is the Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning of Tanggamus Regency. 9. Sub-district is the working area of the sub-district head as a regional apparatus of Tanggamus regency
10. Village or called Pekon, hereinafter referred to as village/pekon, is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage the interests of the local community, based on origins and customs that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 11. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb. 12. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the State. 13. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 15. Guardian is a parent or body that in fact exercises custody as a parent over a child. 16. Woman is a human being who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth and breastfeed. 17. Child Marriage is a marriage conducted through civil, religious or customary law with or without registration or official consent where one or both partners are children under the age of 18 years. 18. Children in Need of Special Protection hereinafter abbreviated as AMPK are Children in need of special protection. 19. Worst Forms of Child Labor hereinafter referred to as BPTA is the worst forms of child labor. 20. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 21. Street child is a child whose life is irregular by spending most of his/her time outside the home to earn a living on the streets or in public places. 22. Child with disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental obstacles that interfere with his/her growth and development naturally. 23. Gifted child is a child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 24. Child in conflict with the law is a child in conflict with the law, a child who is a victim of a criminal act, and a child who is a witness to a criminal act. 25. Adopted Child is a Child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the Family of Parents, legal Guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education and raising of the Child into the environment of the Family of adoptive Parents based on a court decision or determination. 26. Foster Child is a Child who is cared for by a person or institution to be provided with guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health because the Parents or one of the Parents is unable to guarantee the proper growth and development of the Child. 27. Child economically exploited is an action with or without the consent of the child who is a victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual exploitation, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of children by other parties to obtain material benefits. 28. Child sexually exploited is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of children to obtain benefits, including but limited to all activities of prostitution and sexual abuse. 29. Child labor is children both boys and girls who are involved in economic activities that interfere with or hinder the growth and development process and are dangerous to the physical and mental health of children. 30. Custody is the power of Parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect and develop Children in accordance with the religion they profess and in accordance with their abilities, talents, and interests. 31. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government and regional government. 32.

Article 5

Physical violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

Article 15

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and the community as referred to in Article 13 letters b and c, shall be implemented in the form of participation of the private sector and the community.
2. The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. Preventing acts of violence against women and children;
b. Providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and
c. Participating in the handling of victims of violence.
3. The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VII

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

Prevention of violence against women and children

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 13 letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

CHAPTER XII

SANCTIONS

Article 32

In the event of violence against Women and Children, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 8

Neglect as referred to in Article 4 letter d includes:
a. Acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood and care to such women.
b. Acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care.
c. Acts of deliberately neglecting to care for or look after children as they should, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care.

Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 33. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 34. Protection is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 35. Protection of women is any effort made to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. 36. Implementation of Child Protection is a series of activities carried out by the Regional Government, community, and parents, aimed at preventing, reducing risks, and handling victims of acts of violence, exploitation, abuse and neglect of children. 37. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, be healthy, intelligent, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination. 38. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic, social exploitation including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 39. Violence Against Children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, and psychologically. 40. Violence Against Women and Children in the Household is any act against a woman and child that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, economically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household. 41. Exploitation of Children is any act involving children in activities that can harm the welfare and growth and development or endanger the safety of children with the aim of enabling others to obtain economic, sexual, social, or political benefits, including if there is a restriction or elimination of opportunities for children to obtain their rights. 42. Child Abuse is any action against a child, including placing the child in a situation that can cause adverse effects on the welfare, safety, dignity and development of the child. 43. Assistance is social work that has professional competence in its field. 44. Child Neglect is any act of neglecting the fulfillment of basic needs, care, and maintenance that interferes with or hinders the growth and development of children, including leaving children in dangerous situations. 45. Prevention is the effort of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, abuse, exploitation and neglect of children. 46. Risk Reduction is early action towards children and their families who are in vulnerable situations or at risk of experiencing various forms of violence, abuse, exploitation, and neglect. 47. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of children who are victims of violence, abuse, exploitation, and or neglect. 48. Care Environment is care by parents and care outside parental care. Care outside parental care consists of care by foster parents or adoptive parents as well as care in institutions such as orphanages or social care institutions for children or other similar names. 49. PATBM is a movement of networks or citizen groups at the community level working in a coordinated manner to achieve child protection goals. 50. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJPD is a regional development planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years. 51. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJMD is a regional development planning document for a period of 5 (five) years. 52. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards. 53. Child Participation Forum / Regional child forum is an organization that accommodates the aspirations of children and/or groups of children in Tanggamus Regency. 54. Repatriation is an Effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or receiving area to the area of origin. 55. Social reintegration is an Effort to reunite witnesses and/or victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for witnesses and/or victims. 56. Women's Protection Service Provider Institution is a government-owned institution or legally incorporated community institution that carries out efforts to Protect Women from violence, both in the implementation of policies, activities, and administration in service delivery
57. Child Social Welfare Institution is a social organization or social association that implements Child Social Welfare Administration formed by the community, whether legally incorporated or not. 58. Alternative care is child care carried out by Child Social Welfare Institutions. 59. Child participation is the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes related to their lives either directly or indirectly carried out with the consent and will of the child based on awareness and understanding. 60.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26

2. Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

Article 6

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 4 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.

Article 16

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 13 letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 8

Neglect as referred to in Article 4 letter d includes:
a. Acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood and care to such women.
b. Acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care.
c. Acts of deliberately neglecting to care for or look after children as they should, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

REGENT OF TANGGAMUS,

Considering:

a. that in order to protect the constitutional rights of women and children in accordance with the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the Regional Government is obliged to be responsible for the implementation of protection for women and children against acts of violence; b. that to meet the indicators for the Implementation of Child-Friendly Regency, concerning protection services, prevention of violence against women and children, regulations are needed to regulate the various roles of regional apparatus institutions and other institutions; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, and letter b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children; In View of:

Article 17

Sufficiently Clear.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

5. Implementation of guidance and supervision towards women and children who become victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3) and paragraph (4) is carried out through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 13 letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

Article 6

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 4 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.

Article 5

Physical violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 28

1. The regional government implements Guidance and Supervision carried out by means of:
a. Coordination;
b. Guidance;
c. Education and Training;
d. Monitoring and Evaluation.

3. Implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b towards women and children who become victims through guidance on religious values and social values, Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance by the Regional Apparatus in charge together with other related Agencies.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER XII

SANCTIONS

Article 32

In the event of violence against Women and Children, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 10

1. Other violence as referred to in Article 4 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
2. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether or not using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
3. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 28

1. The regional government implements Guidance and Supervision carried out by means of:
a. Coordination;
b. Guidance;
c. Education and Training;
d. Monitoring and Evaluation.
2. Implementation of coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out among stakeholders cross-sectorally with Regional Apparatus, and Community institutions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. Implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b towards women and children who become victims through guidance on religious values and social values, Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance by the Regional Apparatus in charge together with other related Agencies.
4. Implementation of education and training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is provided to women and children who become victims as an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women and children in fulfilling their rights and life needs by the Regional Apparatus in charge, Vocational Training Centers and other related Agencies.
5. Implementation of guidance and supervision towards women and children who become victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3) and paragraph (4) is carried out through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

Article 5

Physical violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs and the interests of the local community on its own initiative based on community aspirations within the system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 2. 6. 10. I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Part Three

Service Principles

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 23

1. The implementation of assistance as referred to in Article 21 includes all integrated efforts to restore and strengthen the condition of victims, carried out by health workers, education, police, prosecutors, courts, advocates, social workers, assistance volunteers and spiritual counselors.
2. Assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 15

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and the community as referred to in Article 13 letters b and c, shall be implemented in the form of participation of the private sector and the community.
2. The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. Preventing acts of violence against women and children;
b. Providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and
c. Participating in the handling of victims of violence.
3. The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

REGENT OF TANGGAMUS,

CHAPTER XII

SANCTIONS

Article 32

In the event of violence against Women and Children, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 28

1. The regional government implements Guidance and Supervision carried out by means of:
a. Coordination;
b. Guidance;
c. Education and Training;
d. Monitoring and Evaluation.
2. Implementation of coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out among stakeholders cross-sectorally with Regional Apparatus, and Community institutions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. Implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b towards women and children who become victims through guidance on religious values and social values, Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance by the Regional Apparatus in charge together with other related Agencies.
4. Implementation of education and training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is provided to women and children who become victims as an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women and children in fulfilling their rights and life needs by the Regional Apparatus in charge, Vocational Training Centers and other related Agencies.
5. Implementation of guidance and supervision towards women and children who become victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3) and paragraph (4) is carried out through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

Article 24

The provision of services to victims shall be carried out with principles, including free of charge, fast, safe, empathetic, non-discriminatory, easily accessible and confidential.

3. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Part two

Forms and Mechanisms of Services for Violence Against Women and Children

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Part Three

Service Principles

Article 15

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and the community as referred to in Article 13 letters b and c, shall be implemented in the form of participation of the private sector and the community.
2. The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. Preventing acts of violence against women and children;
b. Providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and
c. Participating in the handling of victims of violence.
3. The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 28

1. The regional government implements Guidance and Supervision carried out by means of:
a. Coordination;
b. Guidance;
c. Education and Training;
d. Monitoring and Evaluation.
2. Implementation of coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out among stakeholders cross-sectorally with Regional Apparatus, and Community institutions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. Implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b towards women and children who become victims through guidance on religious values and social values, Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance by the Regional Apparatus in charge together with other related Agencies.
4. Implementation of education and training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is provided to women and children who become victims as an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women and children in fulfilling their rights and life needs by the Regional Apparatus in charge, Vocational Training Centers and other related Agencies.
5. Implementation of guidance and supervision towards women and children who become victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3) and paragraph (4) is carried out through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

Business Sector

Article 9

a. Acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. Acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits.

Article 10

1. Other violence as referred to in Article 4 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
2. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether or not using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
3. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

c. Acts of deliberately neglecting to care for or look after children as they should, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 28

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 23

1. The implementation of assistance as referred to in Article 21 includes all integrated efforts to restore and strengthen the condition of victims, carried out by health workers, education, police, prosecutors, courts, advocates, social workers, assistance volunteers and spiritual counselors.
2. Assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

NUMBER 2 OF 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

REGENT OF TANGGAMUS,

Considering:

a. that in order to protect the constitutional rights of women and children in accordance with the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the Regional Government is obliged to be responsible for the implementation of protection for women and children against acts of violence; b. that to meet the indicators for the Implementation of Child-Friendly Regency, concerning protection services, prevention of violence against women and children, regulations are needed to regulate the various roles of regional apparatus institutions and other institutions; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, and letter b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children; In View of:

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.
