CHAPTER VII

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

Prevention of violence against women and children

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 23

1. The implementation of assistance as referred to in Article 21 includes all integrated efforts to restore and strengthen the condition of victims, carried out by health workers, education, police, prosecutors, courts, advocates, social workers, assistance volunteers and spiritual counselors.
2. Assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

Article 10

1. Other violence as referred to in Article 4 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
2. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether or not using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
3. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 6

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 4 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.

REGENT OF TANGGAMUS

HAS DECIDED:

To Establish:

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY CONCERNING IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 28

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

Prevention of violence against women and children

Article 15

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and the community as referred to in Article 13 letters b and c, shall be implemented in the form of participation of the private sector and the community.
2. The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. Preventing acts of violence against women and children;

Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 33. Protection is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 35. Protection of women is any effort made to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. 36. Implementation of Child Protection is a series of activities carried out by the Regional Government, community, and parents, aimed at preventing, reducing risks, and handling victims of acts of violence, exploitation, abuse and neglect of children. 37. Social reintegration is an Effort to reunite witnesses and/or victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for witnesses and/or victims. 56. Women's Protection Service Provider Institution is a government-owned institution or legally incorporated community institution that carries out efforts to Protect Women from violence, both in the implementation of policies, activities, and administration in service delivery
57. I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER VII

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

Prevention of violence against women and children

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

Article 28

a. Coordination;
b. Guidance;
c. Education and Training;
d. Monitoring and Evaluation.

3. Implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b towards women and children who become victims through guidance on religious values and social values, Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance by the Regional Apparatus in charge together with other related Agencies.
4. Implementation of education and training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is provided to women and children who become victims as an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women and children in fulfilling their rights and life needs by the Regional Apparatus in charge, Vocational Training Centers and other related Agencies.
5. Implementation of guidance and supervision towards women and children who become victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3) and paragraph (4) is carried out through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 28

1. The regional government implements Guidance and Supervision carried out by means of:
a. Coordination;
b. Guidance;
c. Education and Training;
d. Monitoring and Evaluation.
2. Implementation of coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out among stakeholders cross-sectorally with Regional Apparatus, and Community institutions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. Implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b towards women and children who become victims through guidance on religious values and social values, Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance by the Regional Apparatus in charge together with other related Agencies.
4. Implementation of education and training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is provided to women and children who become victims as an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women and children in fulfilling their rights and life needs by the Regional Apparatus in charge, Vocational Training Centers and other related Agencies.
5. Implementation of guidance and supervision towards women and children who become victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3) and paragraph (4) is carried out through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

CHAPTER VII

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

Prevention of violence against women and children

CHAPTER XII

SANCTIONS

Article 32

In the event of violence against Women and Children, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

Article 10

1. Other violence as referred to in Article 4 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
2. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether or not using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
3. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

FUNDING

Article 30

Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD); and

Article 15

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and the community as referred to in Article 13 letters b and c, shall be implemented in the form of participation of the private sector and the community.
2. The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. Preventing acts of violence against women and children;
b. Providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and
c. Participating in the handling of victims of violence.
3. The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 6

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 4 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Child Neglect is any act of neglecting the fulfillment of basic needs, care, and maintenance that interferes with or hinders the growth and development of children, including leaving children in dangerous situations. 45. Prevention is the effort of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, abuse, exploitation and neglect of children. 46. Risk Reduction is early action towards children and their families who are in vulnerable situations or at risk of experiencing various forms of violence, abuse, exploitation, and neglect. 47. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of children who are victims of violence, abuse, exploitation, and or neglect. 48. Care Environment is care by parents and care outside parental care. Care outside parental care consists of care by foster parents or adoptive parents as well as care in institutions such as orphanages or social care institutions for children or other similar names. 49. PATBM is a movement of networks or citizen groups at the community level working in a coordinated manner to achieve child protection goals. 50. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJPD is a regional development planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years. 51. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJMD is a regional development planning document for a period of 5 (five) years. 52. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards. 53. Child Participation Forum / Regional child forum is an organization that accommodates the aspirations of children and/or groups of children in Tanggamus Regency. 54. Repatriation is an Effort to return Women and Child Victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or receiving area to the area of origin. 55. Social reintegration is an Effort to reunite witnesses and/or victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for witnesses and/or victims. 56. Women's Protection Service Provider Institution is a government-owned institution or legally incorporated community institution that carries out efforts to Protect Women from violence, both in the implementation of policies, activities, and administration in service delivery
57. Child Social Welfare Institution is a social organization or social association that implements Child Social Welfare Administration formed by the community, whether legally incorporated or not. 58. Alternative care is child care carried out by Child Social Welfare Institutions. 59. Child participation is the involvement of children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes related to their lives either directly or indirectly carried out with the consent and will of the child based on awareness and understanding. 60.

Part two

Forms and Mechanisms of Services for Violence Against Women and Children

Child Data Information System is the collection, management, and utilization of child data which is one of the requirements in the Implementation of Child Protection. 61. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Human Trafficking Crimes hereinafter referred to as the Task Force is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts for human trafficking crimes in Tanggamus Regency. 62. Child-Friendly Regency/City (KLA) is a Regency/City that has a Child Rights-based Development system through the Integration of Commitments and Resources of the Government, Community and Business World that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and Activities to ensure the fulfillment of Child Rights, up to the sub-district and pekon levels. 63. Parahita Ekapraya Award (APE) is an award given by the central government to Ministries or Institutions, Provincial and Regency/City Regional Governments for their commitment in efforts to realize gender equality, women's empowerment and child protection. 64. Gender mainstreaming working group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 65. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office, hereinafter referred to as UPTD is an organization that carries out operational technical activities and/or certain supporting technical activities at the Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning of Tanggamus Regency. 66. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office of Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Office of Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children. 67. Private sector is Non-Governmental Institutions, Business World and Mass Media. 68. Child-Friendly Health Center is a health center that provides services to children completely and in an integrated manner while paying attention to the needs of children. 69. Child-Friendly School (SRA) is a formal, non-formal, and informal education unit that seeks to guarantee, fulfill, and respect rights, provide protection, and support child participation. 70. Child-friendly Islamic boarding school is an effort to create Islamic boarding schools and their surrounding environment so that children can be comfortable, clean, feel at home, worship solemnly, enjoy learning, playing and interacting. 71. Child-friendly place of worship is a place of worship that provides an environment that is comfortable, safe, and appropriate to the needs of children. 72. Women-Friendly and Child-Caring Village (DRPPA) is a village that integrates gender perspective and child rights in the governance of village government administration, village development, as well as community guidance and empowerment, which is carried out in a planned, comprehensive, sustainable manner, in accordance with the vision of Indonesia's development. 73. Integrated Service and Referral System hereinafter abbreviated as SLRT is a service system that helps identify the needs of the poor and vulnerable based on profiles in the Beneficiary List and connects them with social protection and poverty alleviation programs carried out by the central, provincial and regency/city governments according to their needs. 74. Team for Violence against Women and Children or abbreviated as (Tim KtP/A) on Sexual Violence Crimes (TPKS) is the health sector that plays an important role in efforts to fulfill the right to health services for victims of Violence Against Women and Children (KtP/A), especially in recognizing or identifying cases of KtP/A, providing comprehensive services to victims of KtP/A, including making medical, social, and legal referrals.

Article 26

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 15

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and the community as referred to in Article 13 letters b and c, shall be implemented in the form of participation of the private sector and the community.
2. The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. Preventing acts of violence against women and children;
b. Providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and
c. Participating in the handling of victims of violence.
3. The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs and the interests of the local community on its own initiative based on community aspirations within the system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 2. Regional Government is the administration of government affairs by the regional government and DPRD according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration of Tanggamus Regency 4. Regent is the Regent of Tanggamus
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Tanggamus Regency
6. Regional Apparatus abbreviated as PD is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives of Tanggamus Regency in the administration of Government Affairs which are the authority of Tanggamus Regency. 7. Regional Planning, Development, Research and Innovation Agency hereinafter abbreviated as Bapperida is the Regional Planning, Development, Research and Innovation Agency in Tanggamus Regency. 8. Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA DALDUK and KB is the Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning of Tanggamus Regency. 9. Sub-district is the working area of the sub-district head as a regional apparatus of Tanggamus regency
10. Village or called Pekon, hereinafter referred to as village/pekon, is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage the interests of the local community, based on origins and customs that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 11. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb. 12. Child's rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the State. 13. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 14. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 15. Guardian is a parent or body that in fact exercises custody as a parent over a child. 16. Woman is a human being who can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth and breastfeed. 17. Child Marriage is a marriage conducted through civil, religious or customary law with or without registration or official consent where one or both partners are children under the age of 18 years. 18. Children in Need of Special Protection hereinafter abbreviated as AMPK are Children in need of special protection. 19. Worst Forms of Child Labor hereinafter referred to as BPTA is the worst forms of child labor. 20. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 21. Street child is a child whose life is irregular by spending most of his/her time outside the home to earn a living on the streets or in public places. 22. Child with disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental obstacles that interfere with his/her growth and development naturally. 23. Gifted child is a child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 24. Child in conflict with the law is a child in conflict with the law, a child who is a victim of a criminal act, and a child who is a witness to a criminal act. 25. Adopted Child is a Child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the Family of Parents, legal Guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education and raising of the Child into the environment of the Family of adoptive Parents based on a court decision or determination. 26. Foster Child is a Child who is cared for by a person or institution to be provided with guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health because the Parents or one of the Parents is unable to guarantee the proper growth and development of the Child. 27. Child economically exploited is an action with or without the consent of the child who is a victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual exploitation, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of children by other parties to obtain material benefits. 28. Child sexually exploited is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of children to obtain benefits, including but limited to all activities of prostitution and sexual abuse. 29. Child labor is children both boys and girls who are involved in economic activities that interfere with or hinder the growth and development process and are dangerous to the physical and mental health of children. 30. Custody is the power of Parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect and develop Children in accordance with the religion they profess and in accordance with their abilities, talents, and interests. 31. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government and regional government. 32.

I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

5. Implementation of guidance and supervision towards women and children who become victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3) and paragraph (4) is carried out through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.
